Code-graph indexing has become really slow

Problem (2027-01-11, user report): code-graph indexing has become really slow — project opens and re-indexes take noticeably longer than before. Likely regression source: the all-language coverage work (plan c87093c1, merged) added 10 tree-sitter grammars + 7 language visitors + HTML script-block sub-parsing to the index path (src/codegraph/walk.rs, src/codegraph/extract.rs, src/codegraph/mod.rs), and the finish-gate's forced re-index before symbol checks (BUG memory 1dbb8c66) makes every bug_fixing plan finish pay the index cost too.

Reproduce: time the initial index on a fresh clone (delete .coding/codegraph.db, open the project — the IndexingOverlay shows file counts; time it), and time an incremental re-index after a one-file touch. Compare against a pre-c87093c1 checkout (e0ac5dd) to confirm the regression window if needed.

Fix direction: PROFILE FIRST (timing instrumentation around the index phases: walk → parse → extract → store — do not guess). Candidate optimizations depending on where the time goes: lazy/single-instance grammar loading (are the 10 grammars re-loaded per index pass?), parallel file parsing (is the walk sequential?), batched store writes (per-file transactions → one transaction), mtime/size-based walk caching to skip unchanged files, and pruning vendored/build dirs earlier in the walk.

Acceptance: initial index time on this repo measurably drops (record before/after numbers in the plan); incremental re-index after a one-file touch stays O(changed files); the all-language coverage tests stay green (no coverage loss); cargo test --workspace green.

text:
Close the 340K proxy-cache cliff leak (R20a-c)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5, HIGH): post-R12, 47 requests still crossed the ~340K litellm proxy cache ceiling at 16.3% hit (340-400K bucket: 83.7% resets; daily maxP reaches 408,956). R13 (fill_rate 0.3 + the 340K ceiling minus a 32,768 margin → effective trigger ~300K on 1M-window GLM endpoints) did NOT prevent over-cliff prompts.

Root cause (three stacked gaps, code-verified):
1. Rule-4 skip: when the conversation ends in an open tool loop spanning back to messages[1] (a long single-turn tool run — exactly where context grows fastest), summary_cut_index retreats the cut to the loop start and summarize returns messages UNCHANGED (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338, 437-485); maybe_compact falls through and the request is sent at full size.
2. No send-gate: when compaction runs but cannot shrink below the threshold, the code explicitly continues (src/agent/turn.rs:1743-1750 — "Still over: the kept-verbatim tail dominates..."); the 5-attempt budget aborts only on the 5th attempt, so up to 4 over-cliff requests go out per turn, and the next turn resets the budget.
3. Tokenizer drift: the trigger counts cl100k BPE tokens; the provider counts GLM tokens (~10% higher on code-heavy content) — a 300K-cl100k conversation can be 330-345K provider tokens, and one iteration's tool results plus GLM reasoning echo (policy: never strip) jumps past the trigger between checks.

Fix instructions (R20, three parts):
a. Send-gate at the cliff (src/agent/turn.rs maybe_compact ~:1660-1760): when the pre-request count is still over the proxy ceiling after the compaction attempts, do NOT send the full prompt — either (i) allow under-pressure historical-reasoning stripping for GLM as a cliff-pressure exception (the under_pressure machinery exists at src/provider/openai/request.rs:54 and DeepSeek uses it; GLM's never-strip policy blocks it — src/provider/policy.rs), or (ii) fail the turn fast with an actionable error instead of burning up to 4 over-cliff requests.
b. Trigger margin for 1M-window endpoints (src/config/general.rs:334/343 defaults; src/agent/context.rs:151-163 trigger math): lower the effective trigger to ~280K (fill 0.28 for 1M windows, or ceiling 320K) so tokenizer drift plus one tool batch cannot jump past the cliff.
c. Rule-4 fast-fail signal: when summarize no-ops because the open tool loop spans the conversation AND the count is over the ceiling, return a "skipped: open loop" signal from summarize/summarize_with_interrupt (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338) so maybe_compact surfaces "context over the proxy cache ceiling inside an open tool loop — finish or interrupt the tool run" immediately instead of silently re-sending.

Acceptance: a regression test where a conversation over the ceiling inside an open tool loop fails fast (or strips under pressure) instead of sending >340K; no post-fix request_stats row exceeds the ceiling (verify via the aggregates extraction); cargo test --workspace green with the existing compaction tests updated to the new behavior.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-cache-hit-5-review.md (HIGH-1, R20); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (A3/A4 buckets); executive summary BUG 4.

Move API keys to the OS keychain

Problem (2027-01-09 security review, LOW, optional): endpoint API keys sit plaintext at rest (endpoints.toml / ~/.mnemo/keys.toml) — DACL-restricted on Windows, 0600 on Unix. An OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain) would tighten at-rest storage. Worthwhile AFTER the .git/ sandbox-escape item lands (that one is the actual escape hatch).

Fix instructions:
1. Add an optional keychain backend for endpoint secrets: on load, if a key is referenced as keychain:<name>, fetch it from the OS store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain via the `keyring` crate or equivalent) instead of the file.
2. Keep file-based keys working (default unchanged — no forced migration); add a settings action to migrate a key into the keychain.
3. Multi-platform neutrality: the crate must support both Windows and macOS (the project's review expectation) — `keyring` v3 does.
4. Tests: a mocked keyring backend round-trip; config load with keychain: references; cargo test green on both platforms.

Acceptance: a key stored in the OS keychain is used for requests with no plaintext on disk; file keys still work; cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-security-review.md (LOW-3).

Reduce the 1.4MB request body / prefill cost (L4)

Problem (2027-01-09 perf review — LOW as a comms finding but the #1 end-to-end latency lever): the dominant per-turn cost is server-side prefill of the ~1.4MB request body on the uncached prefix — connect_ms 47-86s on the biggest turns (503-message conversations, ~340K-token prompts). Every turn re-pays prefill on whatever is uncached; the client-side share (build + clone + serialize) is only ~25-60ms plus raw upload. The perf report's in-app mitigation levers: compaction aggressiveness (summarize_at, keep_recent) and tool-result truncation (keep_high=20, summary_chars) — which trade the information loss of truncation against this latency.

Fix instructions:
1. Compaction aggressiveness for long sessions: evaluate lowering summarize_at_fill_rate further (0.3 today) or keep_recent for sessions that regularly exceed ~200K — each compaction trades one cold request + summarizer cost for a smaller stable prefix afterward. Measure with the R21 stats (summarizer rows) before/after.
2. Tool-schema pruning with a CACHE CAVEAT: 25 tool schemas ride in the stable head and are cached after the first request — pruning them mid-session would RESET the prefix cache (a new head = full re-bill). Only change the head at session start (e.g. plan-scoped tool sets chosen when the session begins), never mid-conversation.
3. Keep the CONTEXT_FOOTER stable-prefix discipline (already present) — any footer content that changes per iteration defeats the head cache.
4. Coordinate with the 340K cliff item (211e215e): the send-gate + trigger margin there also caps the worst-case prefill.
5. Tests: compaction behavior tests stay green; if plan-scoped tool sets are implemented, a test asserting the head is stable within a session and only varies across sessions/plans.

Acceptance: long-session turns show smaller prompt sizes in request_stats (avgP trend) without a hit-rate regression on reporting models; cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-perf-comm-review.md (L4); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt; executive summary section 3.

Bug-fix plans lose sub-step progress across restarts

Problem (2027-01-11, plan c87093c1 "All-language coverage: finish-gate disk check + code-graph indexing", kind=bug_fixing): a feature-scale fix ran under the locked 4-step bug_fixing skeleton (reproduce → root cause → minimal fix → verify). A session restart mid-fix resumes against an unchecked mega-step plus a wall of detail text — a lesser model cannot tell what already shipped without re-deriving from git diff, so work gets redone or dropped. The plan would not have survived continuation after restart.

Keep the locked skeleton for small fixes; scale the tracking with fix size.

text:
New-codebase project open lacks progress feedback

Problem (2027-01-11, user report): opening/creating a project on a new, large codebase takes a long time and the UI shows only a static "creating/processing"-style state — the create/open buttons flip to a busy "Working…" label (frontend/src/components/projects/ProjectPicker.tsx:225, the `busy` state at :50 wired to :160/:168/:198/:222) and long stretches of the flow show no phase detail or progress bar. The codegraph indexing pass itself ALREADY has full progress plumbing: IndexingOverlay.tsx (frontend/src/components/projects/IndexingOverlay.tsx) renders a SplashProgress bar from `codegraph://index-progress` events (IndexProgressEvent started/progress/done/failed + the get_index_progress snapshot), emitted by the startup pass (src-tauri/src/main.rs:1547-1605 via mark_startup_index_active / emit_index_progress / record_startup_index_progress in src-tauri/src/ipc/codegraph_cmds.rs) and the create-project seed pass (src-tauri/src/ipc/projects.rs, seed_stores(codegraph_enabled, Some(&progress))). The gap is everything AROUND that pass: (a) the create_project command's own work before/around seeding, (b) the switch_project restart window (the webview is recreated — static/blank screen until the new tree mounts), (c) pre-index phases with no events (project record creation, memory index build/reconciliation at startup), and possibly (d) the walk phase before `total` is known (the overlay shows an indeterminate "…" with no counts).

Reproduce: point the ProjectPicker at a fresh large repo (no .coding/codegraph.db), click Create & open — time each phase and note what the UI shows; repeat with open-existing on a new codebase.

Fix direction: first instrument/map the full open/create timeline (create_project → seed_stores → switch_project restart → startup pass → memory index build) and identify every phase >1s with no live feedback; then extend the existing IndexProgressEvent pattern (or a sibling channel reusing SplashProgress) to those phases — phase-level text ("Creating project", "Seeding stores", "Building memory index", "Indexing files N/M") with determinate counts where possible; keep the overlay's MIN_VISIBLE_MS flash-free behavior for already-indexed projects.

Acceptance: on a fresh large codebase, every open/create phase longer than ~1s shows a progress bar with phase text (and file counts where the codegraph pass provides them); no static "Working…"/blank window longer than ~1s during open/create; already-indexed project opens stay flash-free (no regression to the MIN_VISIBLE_MS design); new event emission covered by tests mirroring frontend/src/components/projects/indexingOverlay.test.ts and the codegraph_cmds tests.

text:
Reap offline browsers accumulating per session

Problem (user report 2027-01-12): offline browsers keep accumulating throughout a session — browser instances that have gone offline (headless Chromium died / CDP connection dropped / child webview closed) leave processes, temp profile dirs, and possibly stale CDP sessions behind instead of being cleaned up promptly. Current cleanup is lazy and leaky:
- `ensure_browser` (src/browser/mod.rs:248) detects a dead launch-mode browser only when the NEXT browser operation runs; until then the dead process + its temp profile linger. Every respawn creates a fresh `mnemo-browser-*` profile dir (~line 288).
- `sweep_stale_profiles` (src/browser/mod.rs:320) runs only at launch time (call ~line 286) and removes only dirs older than 1h — in-session orphans (<1h old) accumulate all session, and while the browser stays alive the sweep never runs at all.
- `ensure_webview` (src/browser/mod.rs:705) reconnects on handler death but only aborts the old handler task — audit whether the old CDP WebSocket/DevTools session is fully torn down.
- Child WebView2 teardown exists (`browser_webview_destroy`, src-tauri/src/ipc/browser_webview.rs:670) — audit whether every offline path destroys the child or only hides it.

Fix direction: proactive reaping — a periodic watchdog that checks handler liveness and kills dead browsers + schedules profile removal without waiting for the next tool call; move the profile sweep to a timer and make it age-independent for dirs NOT owned by a live manager (track live profile paths in a process-wide registry so other instances' fresh profiles are never touched — the 1h cutoff exists to protect them); verify the app-exit path (`BrowserManager::close`) kills the launch-mode browser and removes its profile.

Start with a short investigation pinning down what actually accumulates in the live scenario (headless chrome processes vs mnemo-browser-* temp dirs vs WebView2 children): Task Manager + %TEMP% before/after a session with browser use.

Acceptance: a long session with repeated browser use/death leaves no accumulation — dead headless Chromium processes exit promptly, `mnemo-browser-*` dirs stay bounded, app exit leaves zero leftovers; a regression test covers cleanup-without-subsequent-operation (dead handler reaped by the watchdog; orphan dirs removed while a live manager's dir survives).
plan_title: Reap offline browsers — watchdog + marker-aware profile sweep

text:
Safeguard the WebView2 CDP port against multiple app instances

Problem (user report 2027-01-12): when two or more mnemo instances run at once — both live, both with the browser online (debug builds always expose CDP; release builds with the `enable_browser_inspection` opt-in) — they conflict on the web browser port. The CDP remote-debugging port is hardcoded 9222 everywhere: src/webview_args.rs::build_webview2_args (line ~30, `--remote-debugging-port=9222`) builds the `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` value that src-tauri/src/main.rs sets before the Tauri builder (gate `cfg!(debug_assertions) || browser_inspection_enabled()`, ~lines 60-72); src/browser/mod.rs::BrowserManager::new hardcodes `webview_url: "http://localhost:9222"` (~line 189; the test ctor `new_with_webview_url` at ~222 already parameterizes it); `is_app_url` (~line 990) special-cases `http://localhost:9222`. With two instances, the first instance's WebView2 env binds 9222; the second's bind fails silently (proven in .coding/scoping-native-mix-architecture.md — a second env renders but gets no CDP), and the second instance's `ensure_webview` (src/browser/mod.rs:705) then attaches to the FIRST instance's WebView2 — cross-instance inspection/control of the wrong browser tab.

Fix direction: allocate a free port per instance at startup (bind a TcpListener to 127.0.0.1:0, take the assigned port, drop the listener — or try 9222 then fall back to 9223+ for determinism), pass `--remote-debugging-port=<port>` in the env var, and plumb the same port into BrowserManager (e.g. a `set_webview_url` setter called from main.rs, mirroring `set_webview_enabled`), including the `is_app_url` exclusion. Update hardcoded-9222 doc/UI text: .coding/browser-debugging.md (~line 112) and frontend/src/components/settings/sections/AdvancedSection.tsx (~line 529). Keep the security gate + opt-in warning unchanged (the port stays an unauthenticated localhost port; only the number becomes dynamic).

Acceptance: two concurrent instances with inspection on — each attaches only to its own WebView2 (instance B's browser_navigate/game_snapshot drive B's Browser tab, not A's; netstat shows two distinct listeners). Unit tests: the port-picking helper, build_webview2_args with a dynamic port, is_app_url with the runtime port.

Related: .coding/scoping-native-mix-architecture.md (port-binding semantics); .coding/reviews/2026-12-17-security-review.md (CDP opt-in mitigation, unchanged by this).

text:
Fix TTFT anchor: measure POST-send to first chunk

Problem (2027-01-09 perf review, HIGH): request_stats.ttft_ms is 0 on 99.2% of rows (28,267/28,506) — the metric is dead, so the "fastest agent" goal has no first-token signal and the trace graph's Waiting bucket (connect_ms) conflates network upload with server prefill/queue time.

Root cause: the ttft anchor `request_start` is stamped when the POST response HEADERS arrive (spawn_stream, src/provider/openai.rs:683-757). LiteLLM and the direct providers only begin the HTTP response when the first token is ready, so headers and the first SSE chunk arrive in the same burst — the measured window (headers→first chunk; src/provider/openai/stream.rs:86-88 and the Usage arm ~:278-330) is structurally ~0ms. The real first-token wait (upload + prefill + queue) lands entirely inside connect_ms. Same design on the Anthropic path (src/provider/anthropic.rs ~:1460-1529).

Fix instructions:
1. Stamp a new anchor at POST-send initiation (practically: the trace record's record_created, or immediately before client.post) in spawn_stream.
2. Redefine ttft_ms = first-chunk time − POST-send anchor. Keep connect_ms as-is (response-headers − record_created) so it remains the network/upload bucket; the server prefill/queue share becomes ttft_ms.
3. Apply the same change to the Anthropic stream loop.
4. Update the LlmTraceView Waiting/TTFT bucket docs and comments to the new semantics.
5. Tests: extend the stream tests (src/provider/openai/stream.rs + anthropic.rs tests) to assert ttft_ms > 0 when there is a delay between POST and first chunk, and that connect_ms no longer includes the prefill wait; update any fixture/contract pinning the old anchor semantics.

Acceptance: on a live session, new request_stats rows carry ttft_ms > 0 that varies by model/endpoint (the all-zeros gone); cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-perf-comm-review.md (L1); executive summary BUG 2; .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (the 99.2% zeros).

Parse Anthropic cache usage fields (cached_tokens)

2. Mirror on the Responses API path: src/provider/openai/sse.rs:104 — parse input_tokens_details.cached_tokens the same way.
3. Plumb any new field through the usage DTO/trace recording (src/provider/trace.rs usage recording + the LlmTraceView display).
4. Tests: an Anthropic message_start fixture with cache fields → the Usage event carries cached_tokens > 0 and prompt_tokens includes the cached prefix; an OpenAI Responses fixture likewise; existing usage tests updated.

text:
Cache the Anthropic message history (3rd breakpoint)

Problem (2027-01-09 provider-comms review, LOW): on the native Anthropic path we use only 2 of the 4 available prompt-caching breakpoints (the system head + the last tool block). The growing conversation history re-bills at full input price on every request — a ~10x input-cost miss on direct-Anthropic sessions (cache reads bill at ~0.1x).

Root cause: the cache_control placement in src/provider/anthropic.rs (request build) covers the stable prefix only; current docs recommend caching the growing conversation too — a breakpoint on the last message of the previous turn (within the 20-block lookback window for tool-use), and Anthropic now also offers automatic caching.

Fix instructions:
1. Add a third cache_control breakpoint on the last message of the previous turn (the conversation prefix up to the latest user message), respecting the 20-block tool-use lookback limit — i.e. place it no more than 20 blocks before the end when tool_use/tool_result blocks are present.
2. Optionally add the fourth breakpoint on the final block (the current turn's content) for long-lived conversations.
3. Alternative/complement: evaluate Anthropic's automatic caching (no explicit cache_control needed) — if the endpoint supports it, that may obsolete manual placement; verify against current docs.anthropic.com prompt-caching guidance (minimum cacheable size 1024/2048 tokens, 5m/1h TTL, breakpoint count limits).
4. Tests: the built /v1/messages body carries the new breakpoint(s) at the right positions; the 20-block lookback constraint is asserted; existing anthropic request tests updated.

text:
Close web_fetch DNS-rebinding TOCTOU

Problem (2027-01-09 security review, LOW): the web_fetch SSRF gate validates the resolved IP (rejecting file://, private ranges, link-local 169.254.169.254 — commit 8957b12), but reqwest re-resolves the hostname at connect time. A rebinding DNS server can return a public IP for the gate check, then 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 for the actual connection — bypassing the gate (time-of-check to time-of-use).

Root cause: resolve-then-connect gap — the gate runs on one DNS answer, the connection uses another.

Fix instructions:
1. Preferred: pin the validated IP — connect to the IP directly with a Host header override + SNI set to the original hostname (reqwest via a custom resolver or a pre-resolved URL), so the gate answer IS the connection answer.
2. Alternative: a custom hyper connector/resolver that re-runs the private-range gate on every resolved address per connection (including redirect hops — the redirect-hop gate already re-validates URLs; make the IP check per-connection too).
3. Tests: a hostname resolving to a public IP then a private IP (mock resolver) → connection refused; the existing SSRF tests stay green.

Acceptance: a rebinding scenario cannot reach private/link-local targets; cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-security-review.md (LOW-1); commit 8957b12 (the original gate).

text:
Intra-response reasoning-loop defense

Problem (2027-01-07, fresh-eyes analysis plan 77bf6692): a deepseek-v4-flash turn degenerated — content began by echoing the prompt-tail workflow-state footer (including the literal '</context footer>' sentinel), then the reasoning looped about calling create_plan for thousands of tokens without ever emitting a tool call. Nothing stopped it; the user had to interrupt manually. Repro: switch the model to deepseek-v4-flash, send 'Hello' in an active session, watch the reasoning loop with no tool call.

Why current defenses miss it: the stall detector (src/provider/mod.rs:908-929) fires only on a 90-second gap between byte arrivals — a loop keeps streaming bytes; the repetition guard (src/agent/turn.rs:704-741) aborts after three byte-identical consecutive assistant RESPONSES (turn-level) — an intra-response loop is one response.

Fix direction: add an intra-response loop detector in the turn driver / stream accumulation path (src/agent/turn.rs, src/provider/stream.rs): detect repeating reasoning patterns within ONE response (e.g. N consecutive near-identical reasoning deltas) and abort the turn with a distinct stop reason surfaced in the UI. Prefer structural repetition detection over raw length caps so legitimately long reasoning does not false-positive.

Acceptance criteria: a synthetic stream repeating the same reasoning delta pattern N times triggers the defense (distinct stop reason, UI explains why); normal long-but-progressing reasoning does not trigger it; regression test in src/agent/tests.rs with a mocked stream.

Flag assistant responses that echo the prompt tail

Problem (2027-01-07, plan 77bf6692): the degenerate turn's content began by CONTINUING the workflow-state footer text at the prompt's very end ('All steps complete. If the user's message implies code changes (fix, add, implement, re</context footer>'), including the literal '</context footer>' sentinel — the model treated the prompt tail as text to continue. The app assembles that tail itself (workflow-state block + cache-stable sentinel) but never checks whether a response echoes it.

Fix direction: in the turn driver (src/agent/turn.rs), once early content deltas arrive (or at turn end), compare the response's opening against the injected prompt tail (the app has the exact footer/sentinel text it just assembled — search 'context footer' in src/ to find the assembly site). On match: flag the turn with a UI warning; consider auto-abort/repair (re-request or strip the echo) — at minimum surface it so the user sees the model is echoing, not answering.

Acceptance criteria: a response whose opening matches the injected footer/sentinel is flagged; normal responses never flag; regression test with a mocked stream emitting the footer text as content.

Pointers: BUG memory 'deepseek hello-turn failure — fresh-eyes analysis (2027-01-07)' → .coding/knowledge/bug/2027-01-07-deepseek-hello-turn-failure-fresh-eyes-analysis.md.

Persist user cancels and stop the trace ring from erasing history

Problem (2027-01-07, plan 77bf6692): the failure window was unrecoverable within ~30 minutes. The user-cancelled deepseek request never reached .coding/logs/provider-errors.jsonl (that file carries error/stall rows only), and .coding/logs/traces.jsonl mirrors a bounded in-memory ring (src/provider/trace.rs:1359-1366; write_records_to_file at src/provider/trace.rs:1374-1414 — rows not in the current batch drop past the cap) — the analysis turn's own ~25 requests rotated the failure records (ids 1-3) out before they were read.

Fix direction: (a) append a persistent row on user cancel (model, timestamps, phase) to provider-errors.jsonl or a dedicated cancels log; (b) make the trace file append-only history, or raise the ring cap, or rotate-to-archive, so one busy turn cannot erase the previous turn's records; (c) optionally flush the ring to disk on graceful shutdown.

Acceptance criteria: a user-cancelled request leaves a persistent record; a turn making 30+ requests does not erase earlier records from the file (or archives them retrievably); regression test covering the cancel-logging path.

text:
Back-to-back spawn_agent calls cancel each other's agents

Symptom (2026-09-08, plan ccff0138): four read-only reviewers spawned via four spawn_agent tool calls in ONE assistant message — only the LAST-spawned (model-pipeline-reviewer) survived to write its report (.coding/reviews/2026-09-08-full-review-model-pipeline.md). The first three (memory/quality/performance reviewers) were silently cancelled before their first turn: no reports, no ChildFinished notifications, their tabs vanished from the UI ("nothing displays"). Repro: two spawn_agent tool calls back-to-back in one message; the second spawn's cleanup cancels the first agent before its first Started event fires.

Root cause: spawn_agent_shared (src-tauri/src/ipc/spawn.rs:214) runs cleanup_inactive_subagents BEFORE registering each new agent. Its filter (src-tauri/src/ipc/events.rs:1113) cancels every registered subagent with !h.is_running() — but AgentHandle::new (src/runtime/channels.rs:996-1005) starts running=false; only the first Started event flips it true. A freshly spawned agent whose first turn hasn't begun is indistinguishable from a completed idle one, so each back-to-back spawn cancels the previous not-yet-started agents. N spawns in one message → only the last survives.

Fix direction: distinguish "never started" from "completed and idle" — add a has_ever_started flag on AgentHandle (set with the first set_running(true)) and filter cleanup on !h.is_running() && h.has_ever_started(); a never-started agent is pending, not completed. Alternative: set running=true at initial-prompt send in spawn_agent_shared. Also investigate two same-session anomalies possibly caused by the corrupted descendants accounting: (a) the surviving reviewer's ChildFinished notification never surfaced to the parent (best-effort send, src-tauri/src/ipc/events.rs:1040-1058); (b) auto-continue never parked while the reviewer ran (frontend/src/hooks/agentState.ts:167 tracks spawned descendants).

Acceptance criteria: regression test calling spawn_agent_shared twice without yielding to the first agent's task (deterministic under a single-threaded tokio runtime) asserts no Cancel is enqueued and both handles stay registered. Manual: spawn 3+ agents in one message; all run to completion; each parent gets its ChildFinished notification.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-08-full-review-model-pipeline.md (surviving reviewer); plan .coding/plans/ccff0138.md; BUG memory "Back-to-back spawn_agent calls cancel each other"; related: reviewer finish notifications are best-effort (PLAN 5b46674d).

text:
Tool output strips LLM special tokens (GLM end-of-text) — verify + fix round-trip

From a memory audit (2027-01-07; bug memory 86b9ba9a — no backlog item, no fix on record): the tool-output rendering layer strips LLM special tokens — e.g. the GLM end-of-text token (13 chars; written spaced here so it survives text transports: < | endoftext | >) — from read_files output, test panic output, and possibly agent-authored file content. Workaround at the time: codepoint-dump the content and write via PowerShell; the codebase now codifies building such literals from unicode escapes, never raw angle-bracket text (PLAN.md provider-quirk item 8, transport-hardening lesson).

Why it matters: any file that legitimately contains a special token (test fixtures, prompt templates, stop-boundary configs) cannot be read-then-written faithfully — the agent silently loses the token and writes back corrupted content.

First step — verify where the strip actually happens (the memory predates the GLM stream-guard work, commits 720b039 + f322277c, which cuts boundary tokens from STREAMS by design but should not touch tool results): (a) create a fixture file containing the literal token, read it via read_files, and check whether it survives to the agent and to the UI transcript; (b) inspect the tool-result pipeline for sanitization — frontend tool-output rendering components and any Rust-side tool-result escaping; (c) check whether the serving API strips special tokens from request input (server-side) by echoing the token back through a cheap model.

If app-side: fix the root cause — stop stripping special tokens from tool output (they are data, not control characters), or escape them visibly and deterministically so the agent can reconstruct them. If server-side: add automatic, config-driven escaping of known boundary tokens (reuse stop_boundary_strings, src/config/endpoints.rs) in tool results sent to the API, restored on write.

Regression test: a fixture containing the token round-trips read_files → write unchanged (fails without the fix). cargo test + vitest green.

text:
Between-items auto-compact should respect the fill-rate dial

User report (2027-01-07): `[context].summarize_at_fill_rate` is set to 50% in Advanced settings, yet compaction fired far below 50% of the 500k window during a run-all session. Verified dial map: (1) fill-rate summarization fires at rate × window, capped by `proxy_cache_ceiling_tokens` (340k − 32k margin ≈ 307k) — respects the dial; (2) preflight compaction fires at window − `compact_headroom_tokens` (500k − 32k = 468k, src/agent/context.rs:164) — near-window last resort; (3) the between-items run-all auto-compact (`auto_compact_on_plan_complete`, compact_then_dispatch_next in src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs) fires UNCONDITIONALLY after each resolved item — the only compaction mechanism that ignores the fill-rate dial entirely (by design: "every item starts clean overnight").

Proposal: the between-items auto-compact should change the same dial — only compact when the post-item context is at/above the fill-rate threshold (the same effective `summarize_at_fill_rate` × window the user tuned, including the proxy-ceiling cap), instead of always. Rationale: compacting at ~20% context loses detail unnecessarily and spends a summarization LLM call per item; the overnight-stability goal only needs compaction before the context gets large, and the mid-item threshold backstop still covers items that grow past it mid-flight. Design choice to settle: strict ≥ threshold, a fraction of it (e.g. ≥50% of the threshold), or a small absolute floor (e.g. skip below 100k).

Also: surface the knob→mechanism relationship in the Advanced settings help text (fill-rate control vs auto-compact checkbox) and the README config paragraph. Verification angle: if a compaction ever fires below the configured fill-rate threshold OUTSIDE the between-items window, investigate the settings→ContextManager threading (config → AgentFactory fill_rate) for a non-application bug.

Tests: setting on + post-item context below the gate → no compaction, next item dispatches directly; above the gate → exactly one compaction then dispatch; the gate reads the same effective threshold as the fill-rate path (proxy-ceiling cap included); off (default) → unchanged behavior.

The dial map — three compaction mechanisms, and only two of them respect your 50%:

Mechanism	Knob	Fires at (500k window, your 50%)
Fill-rate summarization	summarize_at_fill_rate — your dial	250k (capped by the proxy ceiling ~307k, which doesn't bind at 50%)
Preflight compaction	preflight_compact + compact_headroom_tokens (32k)	468k (window − 32k — the near-window last resort)
Between-items auto-compact (run-all)	auto_compact_on_plan_complete checkbox	always — no dial at all
Which one you saw: if it fired between the two items (the "compacting…" line in the run-all progress) → that's the between-items one, which ignores your 50% entirely — by design ("every item starts clean overnight"), but that's exactly the "same dial" gap. If it fired at the very end (~250k, right when you sent your message) → that's your dial working: 50% of 500k is 250k — the dial is a fraction of the window, not the window itself. (If you ever see one fire below 250k outside the between-items window, tell me — that would mean the 50% didn't thread through to the ContextManager, and I'd investigate the settings plumbing.)

Should it change the same dial? Yes — that's the proposal now queued. The unconditional reset's rationale only needs compaction before the context gets large; gating it on your fill-rate threshold preserves detail when the context is small, saves a summarization LLM call per item, and the mid-item threshold backstop still covers items that grow past the dial mid-flight. The open design choice (noted in the item): strict ≥ threshold, a fraction of it, or a small absolute floor.
plan_title: Between-items auto-compact respects the fill-rate dial

text:

text:

At the plan's finish resolution, the single-dispatch success arm transitions the pointer-referenced item to Done with NO status guard — even though the item had been re-queued to pending (a .coding/backlog.jsonl edit cannot touch the in-memory pointer), and Pending → Done is a legal row (backlog.rs:478-480). text:
Finish gate: force a real code-graph re-index before "regression test symbol not found" errors

SYMPTOM (live case 2027-01-08): a bug_fixing plan's finish gate rejected the verify step with "regression test symbol 'checkFillContract' not found in the code graph (even after a refresh) — the verify step must record the actual test function name" even though the test function exists in the source. The dispatched agent then "fixes" a non-problem (renames the test, records a wrong name) or stalls.

ROOT SITE: src/tool/workflow/plan.rs:1332-1378 — the finish gate's code-graph check for PlanKind::BugFixing. Current behavior: resolve the recorded regression_test against the last-indexed snapshot; on a miss, ONE incremental pass (spawn_blocking(|| graph.index(None))) then re-resolve once; still missing → the error above.

WHY THE REFRESH CAN NO-OP (src/codegraph/mod.rs index(), :247): the pass is content-hash/mtime based — per file, if stored mtime == disk mtime AND a stored hash exists AND has_content, the file is skipped entirely (:287-294); if the stored hash matches, no re-parse (:312). So when the DB's meta rows say "already indexed" but the SYMBOL rows are stale/missing (partial write, schema drift, a prior best-effort skip at :341-343), the incremental pass never re-parses that file — the retry misses and the gate errors on a symbol that exists on disk.

FIX DIRECTION: before returning the error at plan.rs:1367-1373, escalate to a guaranteed re-index of the suspect file(s): a force path that re-parses regardless of stored mtime/hash (e.g. a force flag on index(), or clear the file's meta rows then index), re-resolve the symbol, and only then error. The error message must distinguish "symbol absent after a genuine full re-index" (wrong test name) from "graph could not be refreshed" so the agent does not chase a phantom rename.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Regression test: symbol present in source, DB meta rows fresh (mtime+hash match) but symbol rows missing → the gate's escalation re-parses and finds it instead of erroring.
- The error fires only when the symbol is absent after the forced re-index, and the message names which case it is.
- cargo test green (root + src-tauri), zero warnings (deny(warnings)).

RELATED: same class as the F10 reindex-instead-of-warn pattern — pending plan 1933acf8 / backlog 42302c2d (graph_search self-healing on stale-index misses; BUG memory 57a0c1fd). Codegraph API: src/codegraph/mod.rs:247 index(), :397 reindex_stale_files(), :520 reindex_one().

text:
Parallel run-all — concurrent main agents, one branch each

Open workitem surfaced by a memory audit (2027-01-07): the parallel run-all research (plan 7251fc05, memory 07db9db6, 2026-12-30) produced a dependency-ordered gap analysis for running run_all with MULTIPLE CONCURRENT main agents, each working its own git branch — but the implementation was never queued. This item queues it.

Goal: run-all dispatches N items concurrently, each on its own main agent + own wt/* branch, landing via the existing merge_to_main flow.

READ FIRST: memory_search 'parallel run-all' (record 07db9db6) holds the full gap analysis and phasing; the plan context is in .coding/plans/7251fc05.md. Verify each gap against current code before building — the research predates several landed fixes.

Fix direction: implement per the research's dependency-ordered phases — dispatch-loop concurrency, per-agent branch/worktree provisioning, shared-state coordination (backlog.jsonl union/locking, per-agent stack.json), UI for N concurrent runs, safety (never two agents on one branch; merge conflicts surfaced, not auto-resolved).

text:
Exclude backlog items from Run-All — deferred checkbox on each card

User request (2027-01-07): a way to EXCLUDE a backlog item from Run-All — a checkbox on the item, suggested name 'deferred'. A deferred item stays in the backlog (visible, still pending work) but Run-All never dispatches it — reserved for manual in-app handling or later re-inclusion.

Design — flag, not a status (recommended): add a boolean field to BacklogItem (src/backlog.rs:131), e.g. deferred: bool with #[serde(default)] so existing backlog.jsonl lines parse unchanged (the file merges across instances via a git union merge driver — the field must round-trip). Keep it ORTHOGONAL to BacklogStatus (src/backlog.rs:181): the item stays 'pending' and every existing status transition keeps working. Do NOT add a 'deferred' status value — status is tied to plan lifecycle (item 45dcf577 semantics; coordinate with pending item 998f85fc 'Clarify backlog resolution' which touches the same semantics). Naming note: 'deferral' already names the in_flight → pending requeue transition in the backlog_status tool — if that reads as a collision, label the UI control 'Deferred (skip Run-All)' or pick 'excluded'; the user's suggested shorthand is 'deferred'.

Fix direction:
- Selection: check callers of next_pending (src/backlog.rs:618) first — filter so ONLY Run-All selection skips deferred items (run_all_dispatch_next :1563; its callers backlog_run_all src-tauri/src/ipc/backlog_cmds.rs:419, compact_then_dispatch_next :1489, on_main_turn_resolved :1776; the drain path drain_run_all_on_main_exit :2253; and start-time orphan adoption — deferred items are never selected, adopted, or counted eligible).
- Run end: when only deferred items remain, Run-All ends cleanly ('no eligible items') via the existing end_run (:148) / enter_planning_if_complete (:298) path — no spin, no error.
- IPC + UI: new toggle command in src-tauri/src/ipc/backlog_cmds.rs (mirror backlog_edit :256 / backlog_retry patterns); carry the flag on BacklogItemView (:65) and the TS BacklogItem interface (frontend/src/lib/types.ts:20); BacklogItemCard (frontend/src/components/views/BacklogView.tsx:291) gets a checkbox in the card header beside the status chip, persisting immediately, plus a visible 'deferred' badge on the card; binding in frontend/src/lib/tauri.ts beside backlogRetry (:1584).
- Agent surface (secondary): let an agent session defer/un-defer too — e.g. a deferred flag on the backlog_status tool args (src/tool/workflow/backlog.rs:198) — so run-all sessions can park an item they cannot resolve instead of failing it.
- Verify the memory indexer (src/memory/indexer.rs scan_backlog :593) tolerates the new field (it should — it parses the same JSONL).

Acceptance: with one pending item deferred, Run-All skips it and dispatches the next non-deferred item; un-deferring restores eligibility; a backlog containing only deferred pending items ends a Run-All with 'no eligible items'; old backlog.jsonl lines without the field parse unchanged; deferred items still render in the Backlog tab with the badge; cargo test covers selection filtering + serde round-trip + clean run end; vitest covers the checkbox toggle and badge.

text:
vitest include allow-list silently skips unregistered test files — add a guard

Symptom (live, 2027-01-07): frontend/src/lib/tauri.test.ts was written and `npm test` reported green — but the file did NOT run: vitest.config.ts pins an explicit `include` allow-list (71 files at the time) instead of the default discovery glob, so a new test file is invisible unless manually registered, and the suite total stays flat (71 files / 1007 tests before AND after). text:
Cover premature turn ends during Planning exploration

Live 2027-01-07 (backlog 5c33e945 audit, third shape): the agent's turn ended prematurely mid-Planning exploration (before create_plan) and the session parked until the user nudged ("why did you stop?"). The auto-continue None-arm gates on workflow_expects_progress() = Executing|Reviewing only, so a premature end in Planning parks — in run-all mode nothing resumes it and the run halts.

Why it is NOT auto-fixed: covering Planning with the synthetic continue note would self-answer legitimate question-waits — an agent that deliberately ends its turn in Planning to ask the user a text question ("Which approach, A or B?") would get "[harness note] continue from where you left off." and proceed without the answer. ask_user (the tool) is unaffected (it parks mid-turn, the tool call blocks), but text questions are a real interactive pattern.

Fix direction to decide: (a) cover Planning only when no question is pending — needs a harness-visible signal distinguishing "ended to wait for the user" from "ended prematurely" (e.g. a last-message heuristic or an explicit agent-side marker); (b) cover Planning only in run-all/unattended mode (the runtime would need to know the dispatch context); (c) leave it and rely on the Parked evidence event (now emitted with reason no_work_expected) to make the stall visible. Evidence for the next live incident is already captured by the watchdog ring (agent parked: NoWorkExpected (wf=Planning, ...)).
note: escape hatch (HOW d899e4f7): the automatic done stamp missed — a mid-verify turn was aborted (3 consecutive tool errors: three file_edit refusals on the protected HOW record) and the run-all gate halted the run at the abort; the None-arm auto-continue resumed the session and the plan (3ddf7041) reached Complete with round-3 verification PASS; work committed as c08c177 + c92c4cf + 8ea23e7 on wt/agenticcoding.
plan_title: Unattended run-all Planning auto-continue — mode-gated coverage for premature turn ends

text:
Run-All re-dispatches items whose work already landed — detect done orphans at the drain

Problem: the run-all start drain requeues orphaned InFlight items to Pending without checking whether the dead session had already finished the WORK — only plan completion (finish) marks an item done, so a session that dies between committing and finishing leaves the item looking unfinished, and run-all re-dispatches it as duplicate work.

Live case (2027-01-07, item 35b94671 "Index-based React keys misattribute row state at the transcript cap", mem-perf review HIGH 3): the previous session (plan 225e0dad, dispatch pointer 9fdbc6be) implemented, reviewed, and committed the fix (eac25dc, since merged to main) but died before finish; the item sat orphaned InFlight until the start drain requeued it and run-all re-dispatched it — a fully-landed task was re-executed (caught by the user before any duplicate edits).

Fix direction: when the start drain requeues an orphaned InFlight item (and/or when adopt-on-dispatch picks one up), look for evidence the work already landed and auto-resolve the item as done instead of requeuing: e.g. the plan file (.coding/plans/<plan_id>) shows all steps complete, or commits referencing the item id exist after the pre-item checkpoint on the branch. Consider also a "work landed" marker stamped right after the closing-sequence commit (before review/finish) so a death between commit and finish is detectable.
plan_title: Run-All done-orphan guard — detect landed work at the drain/adoption

Consumed consistently at three sites (effective_reasoning_effort_for, src/config/endpoints.rs:351; build_request_json, src/provider/openai.rs:1773; resolve_reasoning_effort, src-tauri/src/ipc/config_io.rs:93). Much better than the GLM inline name-prefix check (single source of truth, no duplication) — but still model-NAME-driven, not config-driven: the off-encoding cannot be changed for any endpoint without editing Rust, and renamed/aliased/fine-tuned DeepSeek models silently lose the mapping (instant non-retryable 400 on 'off').

Design principle (user's framing): behavior should key off what is CONFIGURED for the endpoint/model — presence of config — not off the model's name. Name-matching breaks on aliases, renames, and new models.

Fix: add an endpoint/model-level config field (e.g. reasoning_effort_off_wire: String — the wire value for 'off'; absent = omit, the current default for most providers), resolved like stop_token_ids_for (model-level takes precedence, else endpoint-level). Fallback policy is a deliberate choice: (a) pure config — shipped endpoints.toml seeds 'none' on DeepSeek entries, policy function deleted; or (b) config-override-with-default — config wins when present, the existing kind+name policy remains as zero-config fallback so unseeded DeepSeek endpoints still behave correctly. (b) recommended: the mapping is behavior (an enum encoding), not data, and zero-config correctness has real value; the config field handles aliases/renames/new models. Update endpoints.toml examples + README config docs either way.

Note: corrects backlog item f322277c, which described the DeepSeek mapping as 'correctly placed in config' — it lives in code (policy.rs), not config.

Regression tests: endpoint with reasoning_effort_off_wire='none' encodes off→none regardless of model name; absent config + non-DeepSeek name omits off; (if option b) absent config + deepseek-v4-flash still maps to none; an explicit config value overrides the policy default when both would apply.

Advanced config: auto-compact after every plan completion — active only during run-all.

Problem/rationale: a run-all (overnight) loop works through many backlog items sequentially in ONE main-agent conversation. Every item adds a full session of context (exploration reads, edits, reviews, commits), so after a handful of items the context window is nearly exhausted — compaction then fires mid-item at the worst possible moment, or turns degrade/fail on context limits. Compacting BETWEEN items — right after a plan completes, before the next backlog item is dispatched — starts every item with a clean summarized context and keeps the loop stable overnight.

Design: (1) New bool setting (default off), e.g. auto_compact_on_plan_complete, edited in the Advanced settings section (frontend/src/components/settings/sections/AdvancedSection.tsx) and persisted like the other settings (config.toml). (2) The trigger lives in the run-all loop's item-completion path (src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs — where a completed plan marks the item done and the loop advances): when the setting is on AND the loop is active, after the agent goes idle post-plan-Complete, invoke the existing compaction path (Agent::compact_context, src/runtime/agent.rs:853 — the same path behind the /compact slash command) on the main agent and wait for the `compacted` event before dispatching the next item. (3) Interactive plan completions (no run-all active) NEVER trigger it — the setting is run-all-only. (4) Failure handling: a failed or no-op compaction ("nothing to compact") logs and proceeds to the next item anyway — compaction is an optimization, never a blocker; the loop must never stall on it. (5) Optional: surface a brief "compacting…" state in the run-all progress line.

Tests (Rust): with the setting on, the loop triggers exactly one compact_context per completed plan and only while run-all is active; with it off (default) nothing fires; a compaction failure/no-op still dispatches the next item; the setting round-trips and defaults to false.

Backlog tab: in-flight items identified by raw checkpoint sha — show a human-friendly, clickable plan chip instead (user-reported).

Problem: the Backlog tab's item status line identifies the working plan by a raw 40-hex id — the user currently sees 'b3befe9ec4e55b5b2359bab49cbb97663e78257b' for the in-flight item (569b5922). That is the pre-item CHECKPOINT COMMIT sha recorded in the item note by the run-all dispatcher (the resume/rollback anchor parsed by extract_checkpoint_sha, src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs), composed into the user-facing status/note text and rendered as the row's headline. Raw shas are noise to a human: they convey no status or meaning, and they don't even identify the plan (the plan id is a different, shorter id — e.g. 593f4a4e — which the agent's tool results show as an 8-char prefix). The user cannot tell which plan/agent the row refers to without parsing the truncated title after it.

Fix — mirror the backlog title-chip pattern (backlog fef458f1, shipped a0ad7d8):
1. Primary identifier: the plan TITLE. Secondary: a short plan-id chip using the same 8-char prefix the tool layer shows (e.g. 593f4a4e), so user and agent references align.
2. Keep the status indication (status⇔plan-lifecycle semantics, 45dcf577).
3. Make the chip CLICKABLE: clicking switches to the agent window (chat tab) of the agent working on that plan (the main agent for backlog-dispatched items). When no agent is actively working the plan, the chip is inert or opens the plan panel instead.
4. The checkpoint sha stays available but demoted: tooltip or expandable detail ('pre-work checkpoint b3befe9e…') — it is the manual resume/rollback anchor, so it must remain copyable, just not the headline.
5. Backend + frontend: the raw sha is currently embedded in the composed status/note TEXT (the frontend renders the note string; no plan_id/planId appears in the .tsx sources). Restructure to structured fields — plan title, short plan id, status, checkpoint sha, working-agent reference — in the backlog status payload (the 45dcf577 linkage records only the root plan id: src/backlog.rs:80, set_plan_id at :438), and render the chip in the frontend from those fields.

Tests (vitest): the row renders title + short-id chip with the sha demoted to a tooltip/detail (never the headline); status renders as before; clicking switches to the working agent's tab (inert when none); the sha remains copyable from the detail.

Frontend: no transcript windowing — DOM grows linearly over long sessions (arch-perf review LOW; verified).

Problem: frontend/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx:98-100 maps the entire transcript — every entry stays mounted for the session's lifetime, and each streaming flush re-renders the full list (entries keyed by index). Fine for interactive sessions; a problem precisely where transcripts get huge: Run-All overnight sessions accumulate hundreds of entries (tool calls, cards, notes), so DOM size and per-flush reconciliation cost grow linearly and the UI degrades exactly when nobody is watching to restart it.

Fix (either, smallest first): (a) window the render — show the last K entries (e.g. 200) with a 'show earlier messages' expander above (cheap, no new dependency, preserves the streaming path); or (b) virtualize the list (react-window / virtuoso) — better memory characteristics but interacts with the auto-scroll-on-stream behavior and variable-height markdown/cards, so it needs more care. Option (a) is the recommended first step; revisit (b) if profiling still shows cost.

Tests (vitest): with more than K entries, only the last K render plus the expander; expanding renders the earlier ones; streaming text still appends and auto-scrolls.
note: Shipped in d97e674 on wt/agenticcoding (plan 51b12662, 2027-01-07): Conversation renders only the last TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW (200) visible entries with a "Show earlier messages (N hidden)" expander (no virtualization dependency; streaming/auto-scroll untouched). Review round 1: 0 high, 3 low — all fixed.

Descendant tracker lags session completion — complete_step stays refused for a turn or more after every child has finished (live-observed, twice in one session).

Problem: in the 2026-12-30 full-review session (plan 72329f2c), the state-transition gate ('cannot change workflow state while spawned subagents are still running') kept refusing complete_step well after child sessions had verifiably ended: after quality-reviewer-r2's finish notification (report on disk), two complete_step calls failed; they succeeded one turn later with no intervening change. Same pattern after arch-perf-reviewer-r2 finished (report on disk, complete_step refused, succeeded next turn). The tracker (DescendantTracker, src/runtime/mod.rs:266-271; consulted from src/agent/dispatch.rs:169-192) apparently deregisters descendants asynchronously or late — post-session finalization (memory consolidation, event flush) seems to keep sessions counted as running. Combined with the gate's breadth (every state-touching tool — see item 569b5922), the parent's plan bookkeeping wedges transiently at exactly the moment it's resumed to make progress.

Fix: deregister a descendant from the tracker synchronously at session end (the finish notification is already the signal — the tracker and the notification should agree by then), or at minimum treat a session in post-task finalization as not-running for gate purposes. If item 569b5922 (gate transitions, not tools) lands first, the blast radius of this lag shrinks to the final-step/finish transitions — but the tracker and the notification should still not disagree.

Regression tests: after a spawned child's session ends (finish notification emitted), has_running_descendants(parent) returns false immediately — simulate with the FlagDescendantTracker mock pattern from src/runtime/agent.rs: a child that completes leaves no running-descendant entry before the next dispatch-cycle check.

Closure session 5979fe9e re-verified first-hand (A/B + both Rust suites green: root 2025/0, src-tauri 231/0) and reconciled the BUG memory.

Reviewer subagents: report-writing failures are silent and recurring — harden write_review_report and surface report status in finish notifications (live-observed; 2 failures in one session).

Problem: in the 2026-12-30 full-review session (plan 72329f2c), two of five spawned role:reviewer agents finished WITHOUT writing any report: quality-reviewer (deepseek-v4-flash) and arch-perf-reviewer (glm-5.2) — two different model families, so not a single-model issue. The harness 'finished' notification is identical whether a report was written or not ('read its report and combine the results into a plan'), and only sometimes carries a path. Diagnosis required shell forensics (listing .coding/reviews by mtime) while the parent was blocked from state transitions. Prior sessions show the same pattern: episodic summaries record 'initially attempted to write the review report but failed validation twice' and 'the initial review report was rejected because the verdict li[ne]' — write_review_report's verdict-line validation keeps rejecting reviewer-authored reports; some reviewers recover on retry, some exhaust their turns and die report-less. The failed quality reviewer's session summary confirms verdict-line rejection as its failure mode.

Fix directions:
1. Validation feedback loop: when write_review_report rejects a malformed verdict line, the error must show the expected format verbatim plus the received first line, so the reviewer can fix it in one retry instead of guessing.
2. Notification honesty: the finish notification must state whether a report was written and its path (or explicitly 'no report written') — the parent should never need forensics to know.
3. Retry accounting: a reviewer that fails report validation repeatedly (e.g. 3 times) should fail loudly with a distinct status, not finish silently.
4. Cosmetic but confusing (same session): report file date prefixes are wrong (security report named 2026-12-23-*, arch-perf 2026-12-24-*, both written 2026-12-29/30) and notification paths display a non-project root alias (\\?\C:\AgenticCoding\... for the project at C:\AgenticCoder\AgenticCoder — same store, verified identical listings). write_review_report should date-prefix from the system clock, and notifications should display the project-relative path.

Regression tests: a report with a malformed verdict line gets a rejection error containing the expected format; the finish notification for a report-less reviewer says no report; the notification for a successful one carries the project-relative path.
note: Fixed in plan 7da7476b (2027-01-07): verdict rejections now quote the received first line; report-less notifications say "no report was written" and carry the project-relative path; the failed-reviewer protocol (text + latch) fires for ANY report-less reviewer incl. cleanly-finished ones; REVIEW_REPORT_MAX_FAILURES=3 dedicated counter aborts stuck report writers with a distinct error; date prefixes come from the system clock; finish resolves project-relative paths. 8 regression tests (all A/B-verified), review 0 high / 4 low (all fixed), both suites green (root 2031/0, src-tauri 232/0).
plan_title: Reviewer report failures are silent — harden write_review_report + honest finish notifications (5b46674d)

text:
web_fetch: redirect hops bypass the SSRF blocklist — re-validate every hop (security review LOW; verified).

Problem: src/tool/agent/web_fetch.rs — the SSRF gate (hostname_resolves_to_internal, fail-closed on resolution errors) runs exactly once, on the initial URL's host (lines ~161-177). The reqwest client is then built with redirect::Policy::limited(5) (line ~186), so redirects are followed automatically WITHOUT re-running the blocklist check. A public URL that answers with a 302 to http://169.254.169.254/... (or any internal host/IP literal) is fetched anyway. The inline comment at the call site documents this as a known residual; the 2026-12-17 review's SSRF fix (8957b12) covered the initial fetch only.

Fix: disable auto-redirect (redirect::Policy::none) and implement a manual redirect loop: up to N hops (keep 5), each hop re-runs ensure_public_http_url on the new Location before requesting it; on blocklist failure return the same fail-closed error as the initial check; on exceeding N hops return a clear too-many-redirects error. Preserve existing behavior otherwise (scheme filtering, size caps, HTML stripping).

Regression test (must fail without the fix): a fetch whose first response is a 302 to an internal address (mock server or stubbed client) is refused with the SSRF error, not followed.
note: Already complete — fix committed as 58849c7 (2027-01-05) on the wt working branch atop the e20b1df main merge: manual redirect loop (redirect::Policy::none) re-runs the full SSRF gate on every hop, 5-hop cap, reqwest parity. Regression tests in web_fetch.rs (302 → 169.254.169.254 refused, internal target never contacted). Reviews: 2027-01-05-web-fetch-redirect-ssrf-review PASS + verification PASS (both LOW findings fixed). Not yet merged to main — land via merge_to_main.

Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] on extract_checkpoint_sha — the tree's first #[allow] violates the warning-free constitution (security + quality + arch-perf reviews, all three reviewers; verified).

Problem: the uncommitted delta in src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs adds #[allow(dead_code)] to extract_checkpoint_sha (lines ~848-863) — the function has had no production caller since backlog 45dcf577 removed the rollback arm; only its #[cfg(test)] tests call it. This is the first #[allow] in the tree, and its comment block argues for the exemption — a precedent every future contributor can cite. Note: the change is currently UNCOMMITTED; resolve it before it lands.

Fix (either): (a) delete extract_checkpoint_sha and its extract_tests module — the checkpoint sha stays human-readable in the item note and recoverable from git history if a caller ever returns; or (b) restore a real caller: expose the sha in the backlog UI payload (backlog_list already returns notes; a parsed checkpoint_sha field would make the manual resume/rollback anchor machine-readable) — arch-perf review's preferred option since it turns the anchor into an actual feature. Tests: source-contract tests anchor on comments and incidental text — pin them to stable markers (quality review LOW).

Problem: several source-contract tests (the tests that assert shipped source files contain required constructs — e.g. the ones pinning the repetition-guard wiring, the deny(warnings) crate attributes, and provider stream handling) match on comment text or incidental formatting rather than structural anchors. Any comment reword, doc-comment edit, or reformat can break a test that actually still passes conceptually — and worse, a test can keep passing while the construct it claims to pin has drifted, because the matched text was never the load-bearing part. This is the same fragility class the 2026-12-06 status-plan-lifecycle review rounds kept hitting (reword → test break → re-pin cycles).

Fix: audit the source-contract tests (search the test modules for assertions that read source files and match on comment/doc text) and re-anchor each on the stable structural token it actually cares about: the attribute (#[deny(warnings)]), the call site (guard_repetition(, ensure_public_http_url(), stop_token_ids_for(), the fn signature, the config key — not the prose around it. Where the contract genuinely IS a comment (e.g. a documented residual like the web_fetch redirect note), assert on the exact load-bearing phrase and mark the test with a comment explaining that the phrase is the contract.

Tests: the re-anchored tests must still fail when the pinned construct is removed (spot-check by temporarily deleting the construct) and must survive a comment-only reword.

Run-all/unattended sessions must expose backlog_add — a direct user request to queue an item was impossible mid-run (user-reported).

Problem: during the 2026-12-30 unattended run-all batch (backlog 569b5922, plan 593f4a4e), the user asked mid-run to add a backlog item ('plan shows a weird odd id number... add to the backlog of course'). The run-all session's tool surface had NO backlog_add (backlog_list and backlog_status were present) — the agent could not comply and had to stash the drafted item in memory for a later interactive session to queue. Whatever the rationale for the restriction (presumably preventing dispatched agents from growing the queue they are draining), it blocks legitimate user-directed queueing: the user is present and explicitly requesting it.

Fix: include backlog_add in the run-all/unattended tool surface. Options (pick per the codebase's design):
1. Simply add it — the run-all prompt already constrains behavior, and the tool's own description says 'only add items the user actually asked to queue'; an unattended agent following a user steer that asks to queue an item is doing the right thing.
2. If the restriction is deliberate (loop prevention: an agent queueing work for itself), gate it more narrowly: allow backlog_add only when the request originates from a user steer (the steer channel already exists — the item's status note showed 'steer received during unattended run'), not from the agent's own initiative.
Locate the surface construction: the run-all dispatch builds the agent's tool set (src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs / spawn.rs — wherever the unattended session's tool filter is assembled; the interactive session's surface includes backlog_add, so diff the two constructions).

Tests: a run-all/unattended session's tool surface includes backlog_add (source-contract or unit test on the surface builder); backlog_list/backlog_status remain present; the interactive surface is unchanged.

Task: Auto-delegate symbol and memory lookups inside `search`/`search_read` — when the query is better served by the code knowledge graph or by semantic memory, execute that lookup internally and return the answer inline instead of walking the file tree, tell the model it happened, and let one repeat of the same search fall back to plain search.

Current state: src/tool/agent/search.rs (fns shared with search_read.rs) already DETECTS symbol queries — `symbol_nudge` (:583: bare identifier, definition-prefixed `fn X`, symbol-intent `foo(`/`a::b`/"who calls X") and `alternation_nudge` (:529) — but only emits an advisory "prefer the graph tools" note; the walk still runs. `known_memory_note` (:924) is the memory precedent (backlog-id patterns only). Notes are prepended above results and survive end-truncation (`merged_note` :863).

Desired behavior:
1. SYMBOL: when the nudge fires, resolve via CodeGraph::symbol_id/symbol_id_fuzzy (src/codegraph/mod.rs) and prepend a COMPACT graph answer: definition (file::name::line, kind), top callers/callees, then "full 360° view: graph_context(id=\"...\")". Fast-path: skip the file walk when the delegated answer fully serves the query (pure symbol hunt, no glob); otherwise prepend to normal results.
2. MEMORY: when the query targets semantic memory — glob under .coding/knowledge/** or .coding/reviews/**, a pattern referencing those paths, or a typed prefix (SPEC:/DECISION:/BUG:/PLAN:/HOW:/REVIEW:) — run the memory lookup internally (MemoryStoreTrait, src/memory/mod.rs; MemorySearchTool in src/tool/memory/retrieval.rs is the reference) and prepend top hits (title + one-line gist + pointer). 4. ESCAPE HATCH: keep the last delegated query key (pattern+glob+literal) on the tool; if the next request repeats that key, skip delegation and run the normal search. One entry, no persistence.

Strengthen backlog item status semantics: tie item status to the plan lifecycle so items stop landing in `failed` spuriously.

Problem: items get marked `failed` for no good reason — a session ending, an interruption, a sub-plan pause, or the agent simply not finishing all surface as `failed`. Failure must mean exactly one thing: the plan was abandoned. Evidence: the 2026-12-29 merge review flagged item 3f3044b9 flipping to `failed` as mere "transient bookkeeping from the prior failed attempt"; an earlier bug (TurnResolveLatch deferred-success, plan 323df14b) already fixed items being marked failed when the work was actually done — the spurious-failed surface is bigger than that one latch.

Desired model — status ⇔ plan lifecycle:
- `in_flight` ⇔ a plan dispatched for the item is ACTIVE. It stays in_flight through interruptions, steering pauses, and sub-plan pushes: a sub-plan always pops back to its parent, so the parent plan is active the whole time and the item never leaves in_flight.
- `done` ⇔ the plan reached Complete (finish). Make this explicit: plan completion DEFINES item completion — drive it from the plan-finish event rather than a manual backlog_status call where feasible.
- `failed` ⇔ ONLY when the plan is abandoned (abandon_plan) or an explicit dead end (cant_resolve). Never on session end, crash, interrupt, deferral, or requeue (the deliberate in_flight → pending deferral stays).

1. Trace and list every code path that sets status `failed` or `done` (src/backlog.rs, ipc handlers, the run-all dispatch flow, finish/abandon sequences, TurnResolveLatch).
2. Make the item↔plan linkage explicit: when a plan is created/dispatched for a backlog item, record the plan id on the item (or a side mapping) so status can be derived from plan events.
3. Drive transitions from plan lifecycle events: plan active → in_flight; plan Complete → done; plan abandoned → failed. Remove/restrict every spurious setter found in (1).
4. Update the backlog_status tool docs/schema to document the plan-tied contract (failed = plan abandoned; done = plan Complete; in_flight = plan active).

search tool: locating files under .coding/ (reviews/knowledge) by content or name is unreliable — three failure modes observed live.

Observed 2026-12-29 (full-review session, plan 72329f2c), while trying to locate reviewer report files in .coding/reviews/:
1. Auto-delegation over-trigger: searches with a .coding/reviews glob (e.g. pattern '## Verdict:') auto-delegate to memory_search even when the intent is a plain file listing. The documented escape — 're-issue this exact search to get the plain file search instead' — does not work reliably: the identical search auto-delegated again on re-issue (observed twice). The auto-delegation heuristic (backlog b804012f) should not re-intercept a query the agent has already seen delegated, and arguably should not intercept literal content patterns that clearly target file bytes (e.g. '## Verdict:') rather than memory-shaped queries.
2. Stale content index false negatives: a literal search for 'bf0f71c' with glob .coding/reviews/*.md returned 'no matches found (engine: index; 1826 files indexed)' although .coding/reviews/2026-12-23-security-review.md contains that string (written minutes earlier). The index does not cover newly written .coding/ files, and the engine silently prefers it over a walk — a false negative with no staleness notice.
3. Result cap + display truncation: the '## Verdict:' listing matched 100 files with 'and more matches', and the displayed output was additionally truncated for context efficiency — making it impossible to enumerate a directory's files reliably via search.

Fix directions: (a) make the auto-delegation bypass sticky per exact query (once bypassed in-session, never re-delegate the identical query); (b) when the content index predates a matched file's mtime — or the glob targets .coding/ — prefer a walk or emit the staleness note and walk; (c) consider a dedicated list-files affordance (or let read_files accept a directory path and return a listing) so 'what files are in this dir' does not require search gymnastics.

Run-All: pre-item checkpoint can commit directly to main — add a branch guard before checkpointing (security review MEDIUM; verified).

Problem: run_all_dispatch_next (src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs:962-984) calls checkpoint() before dispatching the next backlog item, and checkpoint_impl (src/project/git_ops.rs:104-123) runs git add -A + git commit on whatever branch is checked out — no branch check. The per-directory wt/* auto-fork only happens later inside create_plan (ensure_work_branch, git_ops.rs:588-642). So when the session sits on main — e.g. right after merge_to_main lands a branch — the next Run-All tick commits the dirty tree (typically .coding/backlog.jsonl status flips) straight to main, violating the never-commit-to-main constitution.

Fix: in run_all_dispatch_next, before checkpoint(): if the current branch is main, call ensure_work_branch first (fork/reuse the per-directory wt/* branch, matching create_plan's auto-fork semantics) so the checkpoint chain lands on the working branch; or skip the checkpoint with a logged note if forking is undesirable there. Preferred: ensure_work_branch — keeps the resume/rollback chain intact.

note: Resolved by plan a91e71d3 (commits e3977d6 + 97c6ae9 on wt/agenticcoding): the Run-All pre-item checkpoint now forks/reuses the per-directory wt/* work branch before committing (checkpoint_on_work_branch — the same auto-fork semantics create_plan applies), so a session sitting on main (e.g. right after merge_to_main lands a branch) never commits the dirty tree to main; a refused fork (dirty paths outside .coding/) stops the run through the existing checkpoint-failure path — the item stays Pending with the reason in its note. Fix the app-runtime bug: user-interrupted turns silently drop in-flight tool calls (user request 2026-12-30). IMPORTANT: plan this as a NORMAL implementation plan, NOT kind:bug_fixing — the locked reproduce→regression-test skeleton fits poorly because reproduction is a timing-dependent race (a user message arriving mid-tool-batch); structure the work as audit → design decision → implement → deterministic tests instead.

SYMPTOM: when a user message arrives while a turn's tool calls are in flight, some or all calls silently never execute — no result block, no error; the call text can even surface/echo in the user's next message. Execution within an interrupted batch is NONDETERMINISTIC: in one instance a shell call in the batch ran and returned results while the sibling backlog_add never executed or persisted.

OBSERVED INSTANCES (all 2026-12-30, session on wt/agenticcoding, plan 2a3b35d8):
1. Batch [backlog_status + file_write(append to InputBar.test.ts)] interrupted → file_write never landed (file verified unchanged); re-applied later.
2. Batch [backlog_add + shell(npm test)] → shell EXECUTED (results returned) but the backlog_add never persisted — git diff of .coding/backlog.jsonl later showed the item absent; the lost request had to be recovered by planning the feature directly.
3. Lone complete_step interrupted → workflow state still showed the step incomplete; re-issue succeeded.
4. Lone read_files(review report) interrupted → call text echoed into the user's follow-up message; report unread until re-issued.
5. Batch [search + graph_search + read_files] interrupted → no results delivered at all.

EVIDENCE + PRIOR ART: knowledge file .coding/knowledge/bug/2026-12-30-interrupted-turns-silently-drop-in-flight-tool-c.md (committed f556a3d) + BUG memory of the same title. Related fixed turn-lifecycle bug: TurnResolveLatch deferred-success (backlog items marked failed when work done — memory c50b7390) — the turn-resolution area is bug-prone; audit it.

HYPOTHESES (unconfirmed): (a) an incoming user message aborts the in-flight turn and pending tool calls are cancelled before execution (or their results discarded) with no cancellation result surfaced; (b) already-started calls run to completion but result delivery is dropped; (c) the frontend renders/echoes interrupted assistant content including raw tool-call JSON.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: no tool call may vanish without a result (success, error, OR explicit cancellation) — the agent's context must reflect what actually ran; bookkeeping mutations (memory_*, backlog_*, complete_step) either complete or visibly fail. DESIGN DECISION to make explicitly: graceful drain (let in-flight calls finish, deliver results, then start the new turn) vs clean cancel (abort with visible cancellation results) — or a hybrid (drain fast calls, cancel slow ones with results).

TEST STRATEGY: deterministic unit tests around the turn-resolution/abort path with injected interruption points (before dispatch / mid-batch / mid-call); the live race can't be reproduced end-to-end deterministically — which is exactly why this is a normal plan.

STARTING POINTS: src/runtime/turn_resolve.rs::TurnResolveLatch (:48-206, turn resolution — prior deferred-success bug here); the tool dispatch loop in src/agent/loop_impl.rs; interrupt-aware cancellation precedent src/agent/context.rs::summarize_with_interrupt_aborts_on_interrupt (:1318) and ::summarize_with_interrupt_aborts_on_cancel (:1351) — the pattern to extend to tool dispatch; frontend mid-turn submission: InputBar.tsx handleSend (sendPrompt / sendSuggestion paths).

Subagents must not inherit the main plan's workflow state — skip load_latest() for parented subagents (root-cause hardening behind the !is_subagent auto-continue guard, plan 75deaec0).

PROBLEM: tool-spawned subagents share the main plans dir, and Workflow::load_latest() (AgentLoopFactory build_inner, src/agent/factory.rs ~:603-612) derives their workflow state from the main plan on disk: unchecked steps → Executing, complete + unreviewed → Reviewing. A single-task subagent (e.g. a closing-sequence reviewer) therefore sees "progress expected" in its own loop. That state-sharing surprise is what made the auto-continue gate dangerous for subagents: on 2026-12-31 a finished reviewer self-continued through the full MAX_AUTO_CONTINUE=12 synthetic-turn plateau (token burn, deliverable-mutation risk via write_review_report, held descendant-running flag blocking the dispatch state-transition gate) — fixed minimally in ca7c152 by adding !is_subagent() to the gate, but any future gate regression would re-expose it.

FIX (root cause): when parent_id.is_some(), skip load_latest() so the subagent's Workflow starts fresh in Planning — then even a future gate regression cannot see "progress expected" on a subagent. Touch either the spawn path (src-tauri/src/ipc/spawn.rs spawn_agent_shared, where set_is_subagent(true) is stamped ~:150) or the factory build path (build_with_id/build_inner) — pass a "parented" hint through AgentLoopConfig or set it on the factory.

CHECK BEFORE LANDING: get_workflow_state(agent_id) will now report Planning for subagents instead of mirroring the main plan's state — audit the UI/IPC consumers of per-agent plan state and the spawn tests (the parent_in_state helper drives the PARENT's workflow; make sure no test asserts a subagent mirrors it). Subagents already have plan_mutations_allowed(false) (spawn.rs:143-146); this change only affects the state they load, not their permissions.

REGRESSION TESTS: (1) a spawned subagent's workflow state is Planning immediately after spawn (not the main plan's state); (2) auto_resume_does_not_fire_for_subagents (src/runtime/agent.rs tests) stays green; (3) the main-agent Reviewing auto-continue test stays green.
