DESIGN QUESTION (round-3 review §6 of plan 75deaec0): should parented subagents load and derive the main plan's workflow state at all?

Today every spawned subagent shares the main plans dir and Workflow::load_latest() (AgentLoopFactory build_inner, src/agent/factory.rs ~:603-612) derives its state from the main plan on disk (unchecked steps → Executing, complete + unreviewed → Reviewing). Since ca7c152 the auto-continue gate has !is_subagent() (subagents always park on a normal turn end), so the derived state now feeds only: get_workflow_state(agent_id) (UI per-agent state/plan/ancestor staircase, src-tauri/src/ipc/agent.rs:667-693), the per-context model resolver (state+is_subagent based, loop_impl.rs:1009/1076, model_resolver.rs:247), and current_plan (in the reviewer toolset — reviewers read the plan under review through it).

Symptom (live, 2027-01-07): graph_search for `normalize_new_item_text` returned "No symbols matched" — the function was added to src/backlog.rs hours earlier (commit 568d405) and exists at :121. UI event blackout: no Rust->TS agent events reach the frontend — chat, reasoning, token counters and running state never update while the app works normally behind the scenes.

Symptom (2026-09-08, live): fresh start, single main agent, send any prompt. The user bubble renders (locally echoed) and NOTHING else ever appears — no assistant text, no reasoning, tool activity, or ChildFinished; status stays 'idle' with up/down 0 and ctx 0/1M. Meanwhile the work really happens: the LLM answers (Trace panel shows the full request/response incl. the assistant text and finish=tool_calls), tools run, files and review reports get written. Deterministic and total from process start, not a mid-session degradation.

Key asymmetry: everything invoke-driven is LIVE (agent tabs and their resolved names, the Trace panel which setInterval-polls, backlog list, plan progress 'Executing 4/6'); everything that depends on the `agent://event` Tauri event channel is dead. So IPC works and only emit->listen delivery is broken.

Why it is silent on both sides (the trap): `Manager::emit` is a NO-OP returning Ok(()) for any webview with no JS listener registered for the channel — `emit_js_filter` (tauri-2.11.5 src/event/listener.rs:269) looks the channel up in `js_event_listeners[webview_label]` and skips the webview when the entry is missing. On the frontend all three registrations were `void onX(...)`, discarding the promise, so a rejected `listen()` also left no trace. Both are now instrumented: `emit_payload` (src-tauri/src/ipc/events.rs) logs the first 5 emits as `mnemo[emit] #N channel=... agent=... webviews=[...] result=ok|ERR(..)`, and the JS registrations log on rejection ('FATAL: agent-event listener failed to register'). Read those first: no lines => forwarder not emitting; result=ok => nobody listening (JS registration); result=ERR => the message names the cause.

Ruled out already: the provider (one error all day); a dead/blocked event forwarder (agents would stall on the 256-deep fan-in, and they do not); a main-thread hang (no .coding/logs/hang-*.txt); a WebView2 runtime update (newest 152.0.4191.66 installed Sep 5); channel-name mismatch (agent://event identical in src-tauri/src/ipc/events.rs:55 and frontend/src/lib/tauri.ts:32); the event-tag contract (contract tests pass); a stale frontend bundle (target/frontend-dist rebuilt, contains the channel); `enable_browser_inspection` / --remote-debugging-port=9222 (toggled off, no difference); and any code change in the regression window — the only files touched since 11:00 are events.rs (adds a HashMap, no early exits), prompt.rs (comments), codegraph/mod.rs, agent/factory.rs, run_all.rs, none of which touches emit or the frontend.

Prime suspects to check next: (a) the JS listener is never registered or is registered under a label the emit side does not match — the UI is an add_child webview labeled 'agent-chat' inside window 'main' (src-tauri/src/main.rs:217-227) while the capability scopes on `"windows": ["main"]` (src-tauri/capabilities/default.json), and `listen` is an ACL-gated core command whereas app-defined commands are not, which would explain invoke-works/events-dead exactly; (b) `emit_js_filter` uses try_for_each with `?`, so the FIRST webview whose eval fails aborts delivery to the rest — this app has two child webviews; (c) `js_event_listeners.lock().unwrap()` panics forever once poisoned.

Also hardened while diagnosing (keep): the module-level listener no longer DROPS events when `activeDispatch` is null between unmount and remount — it buffers (bounded 2000) and replays on attach (frontend/src/hooks/useAgentEvents.ts).

Acceptance: a fresh start + one prompt streams assistant text and reasoning into the chat, the token/ctx counters advance, and the status leaves 'idle'; plus a regression guard that fails if the agent-event listener is not registered for the webview the forwarder emits to.

Seed run-all worktree codegraphs from the main tree's DB

Problem: every spawned parallel run-all agent pays a full cold code-graph index pass (seconds on a large tree) before its first turn — the worktree is a fresh checkout of main with no gitignored codegraph.db, so every source file is read+hashed+tree-sitter-parsed, repeating work the main tree's graph already represents for every unchanged file. Two independent reviewers converged on this as the biggest single run-all win (2026-09-08 performance LOW-2 lever b; model-pipeline proposal 3).

Files/symbols: src-tauri/src/ipc/spawn.rs spawn_run_all_agent (~lines 140-185, the cold index pass); the codegraph store (src/codegraph/, content-hash keyed, per-file rows); the worktree provisioning in src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs fill_spawned_window (~:3540+).

text:
Fix reasoning leak: stream-level ThinkTagFilter heuristic

Problem (known OPEN bug, confirmed by the 2027-01-09 provider-comms review): reasoning tokens from proxy-served DeepSeek/GLM render in the MAIN CHAT WINDOW as assistant text, including literal think-tag markers. OPEN on main (e0ac5dd); the config-knob fix was rolled back 2027-01-09 (commits 5361db7/38d939d/b05e72d removed — see memory "PLAN: think_tags + vendor policy — ROLLED BACK").

Root cause: ThinkTagFilter is gated to ProviderKind::Local only (src/provider/openai.rs:722). Proxy deployments (vLLM/SGLang serving DeepSeek/GLM) that emit reasoning inline in choices[].delta.content wrapped in think tags — instead of the reasoning_content field — never send reasoning-field deltas, so the parser routes the content as TextDelta and the filter is skipped. The Local-only gate exists to avoid a false positive on OpenAI-kind gateways (a literal leading think-tag in genuine content would be swallowed and rerouted); that concern drove the rollback of the config-knob approach.

Fix instructions (the review's proposed direction — false-positive-free by construction):
1. Replace the static kind gate with a stream-level heuristic in the SSE text-delta branch (src/provider/openai/sse.rs): arm think-tag extraction ONLY when (a) the stream has emitted ZERO reasoning-field deltas (reasoning_content/reasoning) so far, AND (b) the FIRST content delta opens with a think tag (the configured boundary tokens).
2. Proper-reasoning-field models are unaffected by construction (they trip condition (a) false). Inline-reasoning deployments get their tags stripped. Genuine content that merely mentions a think tag mid-stream cannot trigger it (condition (b) requires the FIRST content delta to open with the tag); the existing boundary-token escaping already prevents tool-result-borne tag tokens from triggering it.
3. Keep the Local-kind behavior as-is (always-on filter) — the heuristic only ADDS coverage for non-Local kinds.
4. Tests: (a) a stream whose first content delta opens with a think tag and no reasoning-field deltas → reasoning extracted, not rendered; (b) a stream with reasoning_content deltas → heuristic never arms, content untouched even if it starts with a tag-like token; (c) a stream whose first content delta does NOT open with a tag → never arms for the rest of the stream; (d) the existing Local-kind filter tests stay green.

text:
Classify user cancels as Cancelled, not provider errors

Problem (2027-01-09 perf + provider-comms reviews, LOW): 45+ rows in .coding/logs/provider-errors.jsonl carry "stream aborted — consumer dropped" — these are USER interrupts (Interrupt/Cancel/Compact/Clear), not provider failures. The trace records are marked failed even though the HTTP response was healthy, and no request_stats row is written, so cancelled requests are invisible to latency/token accounting even though the provider billed the tokens generated so far. A genuine stream error can also be masked when the consumer exits right after it.

Root cause: when the turn loop drops the event receiver mid-stream (src/agent/turn.rs:2254-2547 — consume_stream's command fold on a hard stop drops the ReceiverStream), the SSE pump task's next channel send fails (drop sites src/provider/openai/stream.rs:414-446 and src/provider/anthropic.rs:1608-1640) and is treated identically to a provider failure — terminal fail + error mirror — with no distinction between user-initiated cancellation and a real stream error.

Fix instructions:
1. Add a distinct Cancelled terminal class for the consumer-drop arm in both stream implementations: do not write to provider-errors.jsonl (or tag the record cancelled), do not mark the trace failed — stamp a cancelled terminal marker from the trace record's existing timings.
2. Optionally emit a partial request_stats row with a cancelled flag (estimated prompt tokens, cached = NULL, outcome = cancelled) so aborted requests stay countable in the latency/token aggregates.
3. Preserve what already works: partial output IS preserved (record_interrupted_output keeps partial text + tool calls with "not run" results; regression mid_stream_interrupt_sanitizes_truncated_args_in_history) — do not change that path.
4. Tests: a stream cancelled mid-flight → no provider-errors row (or a tagged one), trace marked cancelled not failed, and (if implemented) a request_stats row with outcome=cancelled; a genuine stream error still lands in provider-errors.

Acceptance: interrupting a running turn no longer grows provider-errors.jsonl; the trace shows a cancelled state; cargo test --workspace green.

Cut per-iteration O(history) request-rebuild costs

Problem (2027-01-09 perf review, LOW): every provider call rebuilds the request from scratch: a deep clone of every assistant message's raw JSON (src/provider/openai/request.rs:103 — let mut echoed = raw.clone(), even when the reasoning-retention policy makes no mutation), a full re-walk of all message content + tool schemas for the token estimate (src/provider/mod.rs:710-725 estimate_prompt_tokens), and a full ~1.4MB re-serialization by reqwest .json(). 1. Borrow instead of clone when the policy does not mutate the raw echo (make the echo path conditional on the policy decision; a Cow or enum-owned path).
2. Cache the serialized message prefix across iterations (history is append-mostly; invalidate on compaction/head swap — TokenAccounting already tracks head/tail changes, src/agent/context.rs:709+).
3. Feed TokenAccounting's incremental estimate into the max-token cap instead of re-walking all content per request.
4. Tests: request-build equivalence (same body for same inputs) before/after; a test asserting the clone path is skipped when the policy is a no-op; cargo test green.

text:
Debounce trace mirror file rewrites

Problem (2027-01-09 perf review, LOW): the trace file-writer rewrites the ENTIRE mirror file per coalesced batch during streaming (src/provider/trace.rs:1155-1259 writer_main drains Msg::Dirty then one full rewrite; :1324-1395 write_records_to_file redacted-clones every record, whole-file rewrite; the mirror is capped at 8MiB). Fix instructions:
1. Debounce mirror writes to end-of-stream: the in-memory ring already serves the UI/IPC path, so the mirror only needs the final state — flush on stream completion (or a periodic checkpoint every N seconds instead of per-batch).
2. Alternative: per-record files (a dirty record costs one record's write, not the whole file) — but keep the single-mirror cap semantics.
3. Tests: the writer tests (trace.rs) assert the mirror content after completion; add one asserting no intermediate full rewrites during a streaming burst (count write calls via the test seam).

Acceptance: during a long generation, mirror writes drop from per-batch to per-stream (or checkpointed); trace.rs tests green; cargo test --workspace green.

text:
Cache-affinity endpoint routing (prefer warm endpoints)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5 follow-up — cold-request reduction): every endpoint switch guarantees a cold next request (a different deployment = a different prefix cache). The 429-fallback (merged e0ac5dd) and the queued 404-fallback item (92f1f06f) switch sticky when the current endpoint is unviable — but normal operation always uses the configured endpoint even when an alternate serving the same model id has a warm cache, and repeated fallback bursts (401/404/502 bursts — see .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt C1/C3) bounce requests between cold deployments. On reporting models the residual ~17% resets are dominated by structural cold starts — new sessions, post-compaction, and these switches.

Fix instructions:
1. Extend the sticky-endpoint map (src/agent/loop_impl.rs try_429_fallback :1688-1710, resolve_turn_provider :1193-1204/:1277-1287) into a cache-affinity router: when multiple configured endpoints serve the same model id, prefer the endpoint with a warm cache (the one that served the session's recent requests) over round-robin or first-configured.
2. Track per-endpoint last-used + the session's current endpoint; only switch on failure (429/404 viability) — and when the original endpoint recovers, weigh the cold-cache cost: prefer staying sticky unless the current endpoint fails again.
3. Optional: surface the active endpoint + its cache state in the trace/usage so the effect is measurable (pairs with the R19 tier split + R21 stats items).
4. Tests: two endpoints serving the same model — requests stick to the first; on 429 the switch happens once (existing tests); after recovery, requests stay on the warm alternate rather than bouncing; cargo test green.

Acceptance: fallback bursts no longer bounce requests between deployments more than once per failure; long sessions show fewer distinct endpoints per session in request_stats (endpoint column) without availability loss; cargo test --workspace green.

text:
Plan resumability gate: reject plans too thin to survive recompile+restart

Problem: plan documents vary in crash-resumption quality. On 2027-01-09 (plan be16ea36, file-tool reliability) the user asked "Is the plan detailed enough to be executed after I recompile and restart?" and the honest answer required a manual hardening pass — a resume-hardening context block appended via update_plan carrying the standing user directives, helper paths, test baselines, and resume protocol that otherwise lived only in the conversation. Without a gate, resumability depends on the planning model's diligence that day. A fresh session resuming mid-plan needs: symptom/root-cause context, exact file paths + symbol anchors, test design, verification commands, and any standing directives.

Fix direction: add a plan-quality gate to create_plan and update_plan — the tool layer is src/tool/workflow/plan.rs (existing validation tests to extend: create_plan_rejects_blank_title :2188, create_plan_rejects_blank_goal :2209, create_plan_requires_steps :2171), engine side src/workflow/mod.rs create_plan :451 / create_plan_with_kind :482. A structural validator rejects a plan missing resumability essentials, with an actionable error naming what is missing (same UX as backlog_add's validation). Required elements: non-blank context carrying symptom/root-cause + verification commands; every step names concrete file paths (or an explicit no-code marker for research steps); bug_fixing plans carry the regression-test design (partially enforced today via the bug param + regression_test). Optionally, behind the structural gate, an LLM self-check ("could a fresh session resume this plan mid-execution with no other context?") for plans that pass structurally but read thin.

Acceptance criteria: (1) a sparse plan (no file paths in steps, blank context) is rejected at create_plan with an actionable message; (2) a complete plan passes unchanged; (3) unit tests cover both paths in src/tool/workflow/plan.rs; (4) the gate is documented in the create_plan/update_plan schema descriptions; (5) existing plan-creation tests still pass (cargo test root crate, unpiped, read test result: lines).

Related: SPEC memory 2a009a60 (backlog item detail bar + run-all dispatch enrichment, commit 08a9295, plan 4354296c) — the sibling detail bar for backlog items; this extends the same philosophy to plan documents. The resume-hardening block appended to plan be16ea36 (2027-01-09) is the concrete example of the content the gate should require.

text:
Bug-fix plans under-document feature-scale fixes

Problem (2027-01-11, user feedback during plan 85368a1f): the bug_fixing skeleton is a locked 4-step defect workflow whose plan `context` is written once, BEFORE implementation, from the investigation. When the 'minimal fix' turns out to be feature-scale (plan 85368a1f: parallel wave indexing — new pub types FileMeta/UpsertEntry/ParserCache in src/codegraph/{store,extract}.rs, cross-module changes in src/codegraph/mod.rs + walk.rs, concurrency invariants), nothing in the workflow prompts a post-implementation amendment: the plan file (the crash-resumption doc) keeps describing the intended design, not the landed one; the BUG memory is captured at step 2 before the code exists; the auto-captured PLAN digest summarizes the skeleton, not the architecture. Deviations (NLL restructures, type coercions, fallback paths) and measured outcomes land nowhere durable except code doc comments.

Reproduce: open any feature-scale bug_fixing plan's file (.coding/plans/) mid-fix after a restart — the context describes the sketch; the landed decisions are only in the diff.

Fix direction: (a) constitution rule (cheap, do first): add a 'Documentation expectations' section to agent.md — when a bug_fixing fix is feature-scale (new pub types or cross-module surface), the agent MUST amend the plan context with the landed design (update_plan append: architecture, deviations from the sketch, measured numbers, invariants to preserve) BEFORE the verify step, and write a SPEC memory at finish in addition to the auto-captured BUG digest. (b) machinery (optional, heavier): the bug_fixing finish gate already requires the regression-test name (validated against the code graph at the finish path in src/tool/workflow/plan.rs); extend it to also require a landed-design context amendment when the plan's diff exceeds a threshold (e.g. >500 changed lines or any new pub item) — same enforcement point as regression_test.

The title is available where the id is resolved (the store lookup that validates the id).
